source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus is a 36 MW colocation facility certified for regulated enterprise workloads, not a large-scale AI training site.

The published IT load of 36 MW across SAT2, SAT3, and SAT4, with 295,785 square feet of technical space, is modest by the standards of the multi-hundred-megawatt campuses now being built for AI. Its certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, point to finance, healthcare, and federal tenants. Those are compliance-driven workloads with steady power profiles, not the dense, bursty GPU clusters that make a site matter to AI scaling.

Within Texas, this campus ranks fourth by disclosed IT load and accounts for 7.6% of the state's published 475 MW. That ranking is a statement about disclosure, not about the site's strategic weight: only 19 of 133 mapped Texas facilities publish capacity figures at all. The grid constraint, the interconnection queue, and the actual power available to this site are not in the data. Nothing here establishes whether the campus could expand, whether it has secured additional power, or whether its operator intends to pursue AI tenants.
